title: Prusa MK4 not extruding

sources.title: Clogged nozzle (CORE One, CORE One L, XL, MK4/S, MK3.9/S) | Prusa Knowledge BasePrusaPrusaPrusa

steps.title: What do you notice?
steps.detail: Check if there are clicking noises from the extruder. A loud clicking noise most likely suggests the nozzle is clogged or deformed. A light clicking noise can most likely point to the gearing. Visible gaps, missing layers, or filament curling up and sticking to the nozzle point to a partial clog.

choices.label: GAPS OR CURLING
choices.records: Partial extrusion with gaps or curling

choices.label: NOTHING COMES OUT
choices.records: No filament coming out, no clear clicking

cites.quote: Check if there are clicking noises from the extruder

steps.title: Visual check
steps.detail: Is the filament reaching the nozzle? Check if the filament goes past the Nextruder gear. Is the filament coming out of the nozzle? Pay attention when loading the filament.

cites.quote: Check if the filament goes past the Nextruder gear.

steps.title: Unload and raise extruder
steps.detail: Before you start fixing the printer, try unloading the filament and removing it completely. If you are unable to do it, it might indicate a more serious problem. Also, move the extruder upwards from LCD Menu -> Settings -> Move Axis -> Z-axis or by long-pressing the LCD rotative controller for better access to the clogged parts.

cites.quote: Before you start fixing the printer, try unloading the filament and removing it completely.

steps.title: Filament stuck in tube?

cue.line2: LOOK AT TOP OF NOZZLE TUBE

steps.detail: If the filament broke off, observe the area next to the gearbox and top of the nozzle tube, to assess whether there is filament sticking out of the tube. If it is there, consider skipping to the Pull out filament with pliers technique.

choices.label: FILAMENT STICKING OUT
choices.records: Broken filament visible at top of nozzle tube

choices.label: NO FILAMENT VISIBLE
choices.records: No filament sticking out of the nozzle tube

cites.quote: observe the area next to the gearbox and top of the nozzle tube

steps.title: Pull out with pliers
steps.detail: Heat the nozzle only using the printer's menu. While the hotend is heated to 280 °C, firmly grab the filament with needle-nose pliers. Slowly drag/feed the filament upwards, bit by bit, through the top of the extruder body, until it is completely removed from the nozzle tube. If successful, a cold pull afterwards is recommended.
warnings: Hotend is at 280 °C - do not touch hot parts.
Heat the nozzle only using the printer's menu, not an external heating source, as this can cause damage.
steps.expected: The filament is completely removed from the nozzle tube.

cites.quote: Slowly drag/feed the filament upwards, bit by bit, through the top of the extruder body

steps.title: Push new filament through
steps.detail: Access the top of the Nextruder, removing any fittings. Prepare about 40 cm of PLA. Go to LCD Menu -> Control -> Temperature -> Nozzle and set 260 °C if you used PLA, or 280 °C for higher-temperature materials such as PETG or ASA. After it reaches temperature, wait 2 minutes, checking whether filament starts flowing or dripping out. Push new filament into the Nextruder.
warnings: Nozzle is at 260-280 °C - do not touch it.
Heat the nozzle only using the printer's menu, not an external heating source, as this can cause damage.
steps.expected: Filament starts flowing out of the nozzle.

cites.quote: Set the nozzle temperature to 260 °C if you have been using PLA or to 280 °C if you have been using higher-temperature materials

steps.title: Does filament flow?
steps.detail: If filament flows after these steps, the clog might have been cleared. Attempt some filament loading or test prints to confirm this.

choices.label: NO FLOW
choices.records: Flow not reestablished after pushing filament

cites.quote: If filament flows after steps 5 and 6, the clog might have been cleared.

steps.title: Nozzle may need replacing
steps.detail: If filament flow is not reestablished with these steps, most likely the nozzle needs to be replaced, with the blockage being further up from the nozzle tip. Prusa still recommends attempting the automatic cold pull, though it is unlikely to work in this case. Let the printer cool before handling the nozzle.
warnings: Let the hotend cool down before touching it.

cites.quote: most likely the nozzle needs to be replaced, with the blockage being further up from the nozzle tip

steps.title: Automatic cold pull
steps.detail: Have at least 30 cm of PLA. Navigate to LCD Menu -> Control -> Cold Pull (automatic from firmware 6.0.0 on MK4/S). Choose to unload the current filament (recommended if not PLA), Load PLA filament, or continue with loaded filament (only if PLA). The printer cools to 36 °C, heats to 80 °C and unloads automatically. Finish by pulling the filament upwards by hand; if stuck, open the idler lever. Repeat until the tip comes out clean.
warnings: The nozzle heats during this procedure - do not touch it.
Pull straight upwards, not sideways, or the filament can break inside.
steps.expected: A clean tip shows the imprint of the nozzle and no mixed colour or dark marks.
tools: at least 30 cm of PLA filament

cites.quote: Then, navigate to LCD Menu -> Control -> Cold Pull.

steps.title: Confirm with a test print
steps.detail: The clog might have been cleared. Attempt some filament loading or test prints to confirm this. You might want to repeat the cold pull several times until the filament comes out clean.

cites.quote: Attempt some filament loading or test prints to confirm this.

steps.title: Clean the feeding gear
steps.detail: Filament debris can form in the grooves of the feeding gear, causing insufficient extrusion. Access the extruder by lifting the Idler Nut, then moving the Idle Shaft. Blow away the dirt with compressed air, or use a brass brush or an ordinary toothpick. Use the access hole on the side of the extruder. If the idler tension screws were touched, their tips must be aligned with the front surface of the Idler Nut.

cites.quote: You can blow away the dirt with compressed air, or use a brass brush or an ordinary toothpick.

steps.title: Check the Nextruder motor
steps.detail: This involves taking the gearbox apart. Ensure the printer is cold and switched off, and that you have the PG-assembly-adapter. Remove the PG-case together with the PG-ring, gearbox, and main plate in one piece. Manually rotate the Nextruder motor shaft with your fingers. When reassembling, reassemble the block, then perform the gearbox alignment.
warnings: Ensure the printer is cold and switched off first.
steps.expected: The shaft rotates relatively smoothly, with a slight but uniform resistance.

cites.quote: Ensure the printer is cold and switched off, and that you have the PG-assembly-adapter before continuing with the following procedure.

steps.title: Motor resistance result
steps.detail: If you feel harsh resistance, catching, or a grinding sensation, there may be debris stuck deep within the gearbox teeth, a worn-out gear, or a mechanical fault within the motor. After reassembly, perform the gearbox alignment from the dedicated article.

cites.quote: there may be debris stuck deep within the gearbox teeth, a worn-out gear, or a mechanical fault within the motor
